title: Prerequisite Programmes — PRPs, GHPs, GMPs and SSOPs
shortDescription: The hygiene foundation underneath HACCP and FSMS.
genZNote: No HACCP plan survives a dirty kitchen. PRPs, GHP, GMP and SSOPs are the foundation — skip them and the whole building leans.

sections.heading: What Each Term Means
sections.body: FSSAI Schedule 4 of the Licensing Regulations prescribes GHP/GMP requirements: Part II for general manufacturers/processors, Part I for petty FBOs, Part III for catering/food service, with additional parts for specific categories (e.g. milk and milk products, meat) and for transport and storage.

table.caption: PRP family
rows: Basic conditions/activities to maintain a hygienic environment
Cleaning, pest control, training, supplier approval, calibration
Good Hygiene Practices — hygiene measures across the chain (Codex CXC 1-1969)
Good Manufacturing Practices — factory design, equipment, process control, documentation
Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures — written, site-specific cleaning/sanitation procedures with monitoring

sections.heading: Core Elements
bullets: Premises and equipment: layout, flooring, ventilation, lighting, hygienic design.
Water and ice quality, air, waste management, pest control.
Personnel hygiene, training and medical checks.
Supplier control, receiving, storage and transport; allergen control; traceability and recall.
Calibration, maintenance and cleaning schedules; documentation and records.
Verification through internal audits, swabs and product testing.

sections.heading: Relation to HACCP
sections.body: PRPs control general hygiene hazards; HACCP controls process-specific significant hazards at CCPs. Weak PRPs cause HACCP plans to have too many CCPs; strong PRPs allow HACCP to focus. ISO 22000 distinguishes PRPs, operational PRPs (OPRPs) and CCPs — see the ISO lessons.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: PRPs (GHP, GMP, SSOP and related programmes) are the basic hygiene conditions required before HACCP can be effective.

highYieldFacts: SSOP is site-specific; GMP is general.
commonTraps: Do not treat PRPs as optional.

sources.name: Codex General Principles of Food Hygiene (CXC 1-1969)
